:::{#hero}

My research asks two questions about international organisations. The first is how a rising power changes them. China writes rules, reshapes global policymaking and seeks leadership posts in a way that is at once cautious and ambitious, which leaves much of its behaviour puzzling. I study this through [UN leadership posts](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11558-024-09571-2), [UN staffing](https://doi.org/10.1093/ia/iiab071) and [the Global Security Initiative](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7381159). The second is how international organisations sustain cooperation without enforcement, which I study through [WTO regulatory scrutiny](working-papers.qmd) and donors' earmarked funding of UN agencies.

My recent research extends these questions to China's diplomacy and to artificial intelligence in international politics. I study why Chinese leaders [meet counterparts in third countries during crises](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=6647859), and I benchmark the foreign-policy attitudes of [large language models](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7681466). My work has appeared in the *Review of International Organizations*, *International Affairs*, the *Journal of Global Security Studies* and *Global Policy*, as well as in a Lowy Institute report and *The Washington Post*. My research has been supported by NTU's Supporting Pioneering Academic Research Knowledge (SPARK) White Space Funding and UCLA's Alice Belkin Memorial Scholarship.
